global: NOT medical advice, and NOT responsibility of the author. Everything here is a STATISTICAL ESTIMATE — population-level associations and probabilities from research databases, not facts, not a diagnosis, and not a prediction about you personally. Consumer chips are error-prone and test only a tiny slice of your DNA; most effects are tiny and outweighed by lifestyle, environment, age and chance. The author accepts no responsibility or liability for any decision or outcome from using this; it is provided AS IS, with no warranty. Do not make medical, health or life decisions based on it — confirm anything that matters with a clinician and an accredited lab. Use at your own risk. Your raw data never left this machine.
prs: A polygenic score is a genetic tendency across many small-effect variants, standardized to a European reference distribution — NOT a diagnosis or a lifetime risk. Diet, weight, blood pressure, age and luck matter as much or more.
pgx: Pharmacogenomics is educational only. Never start, stop or change any medication without your doctor or pharmacist. Show them these results if a listed drug is ever considered; decisions need clinical-grade genotyping.
carrier: This tests only a few specific founder variants — NOT the whole genes, which can carry thousands of other mutations found only by full clinical sequencing. Consumer chips misread rare indels; a clear result does not rule out risk. For family planning or a family cancer history, see a genetic counselor for a clinical panel. Especially for BRCA, confirm anything with an accredited lab.
ancestry: Haplogroup and continental-ancestry calls are best-estimates from a limited marker set; sub-population and exact subclade calls need dedicated tools.
neanderthal: A small marker panel — illustrative carriage, not a precise genome-wide percentage.
